newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria's Tlas asks forces in Lebanon to be vigilant.
newsitem.headline: Syria's Tlas asks forces in Lebanon to be vigilant.

text.p: Syrian Defence Minister Lieutenant-General Mustafa Tlas has visited Syrian forces in Lebanon and urged the forces to maintain a high level of vigilance.
Official newspapers published on Thursday said Tlas's visit to Lebanon, where Syria has about 35,000 troops, was made on Wednesday on the orders of President Hafez al-Assad.
"Tlas stressed the necessity of continuing training to maintain the highest level of combat readiness," the papers said.
Tlas's visit coincided with one by his Israeli counterpart Yitzhak Mordechai to the opposite side of the border in the Golan Heights, occupied by Israel since 1967.
Syria's movement of thousands of troops in Lebanon last month from Beirut to the foot of the Golan near the border with Israel caused war jitters in the Jewish state.
During his Golan visit Mordechai warned Damascus against launching any war against Israel and invited Assad to visit Jerusalem.
But the Syrian defence minister accused the Israeli government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of launching a "savage campaign against Arabs" and of trying to undermine the peace process.
"Netanyahu wants to achieve an Israeli-style peace that would ensure security and stability for Israel at the expanse of the security and rights of Arabs," the papers quoted Tlas as saying.
"Netanyahu has proved that he is not a man of peace but a man who sees a just and comprehensive peace as dangerous for Israel," Tlas said.
Tlas affirmed Syria's commitment to peace as a strategic option but reiterated Damascus's refusal to give any concessions to the Jewish state.

"We in Syria are committed to a just and comprehensive peace as a strategic option...a peace that would return the land and rights. We will never agree to cede an atom of our lands. We will not bargain on a principle..." Tlas said.
Syria, which wants full Israeli withdrawal from the Golan, has strongly condemned Netanyahu's hardline government for refusing to trade land for peace.
Damascus has had sporadic peace negotiations with Israel since 1991 but no talks have been held since Netanyahu took office in June.
